ESV.1: “But now they laugh at me, men who are younger than I, whose fathers I would have disdained to set with the dogs of my flock.
ESV.2: What could I gain from the strength of their hands, men whose vigor is gone?
ESV.3: Through want and hard hunger they gnaw the dry ground by night in waste and desolation;
ESV.4: they pick saltwort and the leaves of bushes, and the roots of the broom tree for their food.
ESV.5: They are driven out from human company; they shout after them as after a thief.
ESV.6: In the gullies of the torrents they must dwell, in holes of the earth and of the rocks.
ESV.7: Among the bushes they bray; under the nettles they huddle together.
ESV.8: A senseless, a nameless brood, they have been whipped out of the land.
ESV.9: “And now I have become their song; I am a byword to them.
ESV.10: They abhor me; they keep aloof from me; they do not hesitate to spit at the sight of me.
ESV.11: Because God has loosed my cord and humbled me, they have cast off restraint  in my presence.
ESV.12: On my right hand the rabble rise; they push away my feet; they cast up against me their ways of destruction.
ESV.13: They break up my path; they promote my calamity; they need no one to help them.
ESV.14: As through a wide breach they come; amid the crash they roll on.
ESV.15: Terrors are turned upon me; my honor is pursued as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed away like a cloud.
ESV.16: “And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction have taken hold of me.
ESV.17: The night racks my bones, and the pain that gnaws me takes no rest.
ESV.18: With great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me about like the collar of my tunic.
ESV.19: God  has cast me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.
ESV.20: I cry to you for help and you do not answer me; I stand, and you only look at me.
ESV.21: You have turned cruel to me; with the might of your hand you persecute me.
ESV.22: You lift me up on the wind; you make me ride on it, and you toss me about in the roar of the storm.
ESV.23: For I know that you will bring me to death and to the house appointed for all living.
ESV.24: “Yet does not one in a heap of ruins stretch out his hand, and in his disaster cry for help?
ESV.25: Did not I weep for him whose day was hard? Was not my soul grieved for the needy?
ESV.26: But when I hoped for good, evil came, and when I waited for light, darkness came.
ESV.27: My inward parts are in turmoil and never still; days of affliction come to meet me.
ESV.28: I go about darkened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
ESV.29: I am a brother of jackals and a companion of ostriches.
ESV.30: My skin turns black and falls from me, and my bones burn with heat.
ESV.31: My lyre is turned to mourning, and my pipe to the voice of those who weep.

NLT.1:
“But now I am mocked by people younger than I,
by young men whose fathers are not worthy to run with my sheepdogs.
NLT.2:
A lot of good they are to me —
those worn-out wretches!
NLT.3:
They are gaunt from poverty and hunger.
They claw the dry ground in desolate wastelands.
NLT.4:
They pluck wild greens from among the bushes
and eat from the roots of broom trees.
NLT.5:
They are driven from human society,
and people shout at them as if they were thieves.
NLT.6:
So now they live in frightening ravines,
in caves and among the rocks.
NLT.7:
They sound like animals howling among the bushes,
huddled together beneath the nettles.
NLT.8:
They are nameless fools,
outcasts from society.
NLT.9:
“And now they mock me with vulgar songs!
They taunt me!
NLT.10:
They despise me and won’t come near me,
except to spit in my face.
NLT.11:
For God has cut my bowstring.
He has humbled me,
so they have thrown off all restraint.
NLT.12:
These outcasts oppose me to my face.
They send me sprawling
and lay traps in my path.
NLT.13:
They block my road
and do everything they can to destroy me.
They know I have no one to help me.
NLT.14:
They come at me from all directions.
They jump on me when I am down.
NLT.15:
I live in terror now.
My honor has blown away in the wind,
and my prosperity has vanished like a cloud.
NLT.16:
“And now my life seeps away.
Depression haunts my days.
NLT.17:
At night my bones are filled with pain,
which gnaws at me relentlessly.
NLT.18:
With a strong hand, God grabs my shirt.
He grips me by the collar of my coat.
NLT.19:
He has thrown me into the mud.
I’m nothing more than dust and ashes.
NLT.20:
“I cry to you, O God, but you don’t answer.
I stand before you, but you don’t even look.
NLT.21:
You have become cruel toward me.
You use your power to persecute me.
NLT.22:
You throw me into the whirlwind
and destroy me in the storm.
NLT.23:
And I know you are sending me to my death —
the destination of all who live.
NLT.24:
“Surely no one would turn against the needy
when they cry for help in their trouble.
NLT.25:
Did I not weep for those in trouble?
Was I not deeply grieved for the needy?
NLT.26:
So I looked for good, but evil came instead.
I waited for the light, but darkness fell.
NLT.27:
My heart is troubled and restless.
Days of suffering torment me.
NLT.28:
I walk in gloom, without sunlight.
I stand in the public square and cry for help.
NLT.29:
Instead, I am considered a brother to jackals
and a companion to owls.
NLT.30:
My skin has turned dark,
and my bones burn with fever.
NLT.31:
My harp plays sad music,
and my flute accompanies those who weep.

AMP.1:
"But now those younger than I mock and laugh at me,
Whose fathers I refused to put with the sheepdogs of my flock.
AMP.2:
"Indeed, how could the strength of their hands profit me?
Vigor had perished from them.
AMP.3:
"They are gaunt with want and famine;
They gnaw the dry and barren ground by night in [the gloom of] waste and desolation.
AMP.4:
"They pluck [and eat] saltwort (mallows) among the bushes,
And their food is the root of the broom shrub.
AMP.5:
"They are driven from the community;
They shout after them as after a thief.
AMP.6:
"They must dwell on the slopes of wadis
And in holes in the ground and in rocks.
AMP.7:
"Among the bushes they cry out [like wild animals];
Beneath the prickly scrub they gather and huddle together.
AMP.8:
"They are the sons of [worthless and nameless] fools,
They have been driven out of the land.
AMP.9:
"And now I have become [the subject of] their taunting;
Yes, I am a byword and a laughingstock to them.
AMP.10:
"They hate me, they stand aloof from me,
And do not refrain from spitting in my face.
AMP.11:
"For God has loosed His bowstring [attacking me] and [He has] afflicted and humbled me;
They have cast off the bridle [of restraint] before me.
AMP.12:
"On my right the [rabble] brood rises;
They push my feet away, and they build up their ways of destruction against me [like an advancing army].
AMP.13:
"They break up and clutter my path [upsetting my plans],
They profit from my destruction;
No one restrains them.
AMP.14:
"As through a wide breach they come,
Amid the crash [of falling walls] they roll on [over me].
AMP.15:
"Terrors are turned upon me;
They chase away my honor and reputation like the wind,
And my prosperity has passed away like a cloud.
AMP.16:
"And now my soul is poured out within me;
The days of affliction have seized me.
AMP.17:
"My bones are pierced [with aching] in the night season,
And the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
AMP.18:
"By the great force [of my disease] my garment (skin) is disfigured and blemished;
It binds about me [choking me] like the collar of my coat.
AMP.19:
"God has cast me into the mire [a swampland of crisis],
And I have become [worthless] like dust and ashes.
AMP.20:
"I cry to You for help, [Lord,] but You do not answer me;
I stand up, but You [only] gaze [indifferently] at me.
AMP.21:
"You have become harsh and cruel to me;
With the might of Your hand You [keep me alive only to] persecute me.
AMP.22:
"You lift me up on the wind and cause me to ride [upon it];
And You toss me about in the tempest and dissolve me in the storm.
AMP.23:
"For I know that You will bring me to death
And to the house of meeting [appointed] for all the living.
AMP.24:
"However, does not one falling in a heap of ruins stretch out his hand?
Or in his disaster [will he not] therefore cry out for help?
AMP.25:
"Did I not weep for one whose life was hard and filled with trouble?
Was not my heart grieved for the needy?
AMP.26:
"When I expected good, then came evil [to me];
And when I waited for light, then came darkness.
AMP.27:
"I am seething within and my heart is troubled and cannot rest;
Days of affliction come to meet me.
AMP.28:
"I go about mourning without comfort [my skin blackened by disease, not by the heat of the sun];
I stand up in the assembly and cry out for help.
AMP.29:
"I am a brother to [howling] jackals,
And a companion to ostriches [which scream dismally].
AMP.30:
"My skin falls from me in blackened flakes,
And my bones are burned with fever.
AMP.31:
"Therefore my lyre (harp) is used for [the sound of] mourning,
And my flute for the [sound of the] voices of those who weep.

NIV.1:
“But now they mock me,
men younger than I,
whose fathers I would have disdained
to put with my sheep dogs.
NIV.2:
Of what use was the strength of their hands to me,
since their vigor had gone from them?
NIV.3:
Haggard from want and hunger,
they roamed the parched land
in desolate wastelands at night.
NIV.4:
In the brush they gathered salt herbs,
and their food was the root of the broom tree.
NIV.5:
They were banished from their fellow men,
shouted at as if they were thieves.
NIV.6:
They were forced to live in the dry stream beds,
among the rocks and in holes in the ground.
NIV.7:
They brayed among the bushes
and huddled in the undergrowth.
NIV.8:
A base and nameless brood,
they were driven out of the land.
NIV.9:
“And now their sons mock me in song;
I have become a byword among them.
NIV.10:
They detest me and keep their distance;
they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
NIV.11:
Now that God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me,
they throw off restraint in my presence.
NIV.12:
On my right the tribe attacks;
they lay snares for my feet,
they build their siege ramps against me.
NIV.13:
They break up my road;
they succeed in destroying me—
without anyone’s helping them.
NIV.14:
They advance as through a gaping breach;
amid the ruins they come rolling in.
NIV.15:
Terrors overwhelm me;
my dignity is driven away as by the wind,
my safety vanishes like a cloud.
NIV.16:
“And now my life ebbs away;
days of suffering grip me.
NIV.17:
Night pierces my bones;
my gnawing pains never rest.
NIV.18:
In his great power God becomes like clothing to me;
he binds me like the neck of my garment.
NIV.19:
He throws me into the mud,
and I am reduced to dust and ashes.
NIV.20:
“I cry out to you, O God, but you do not answer;
I stand up, but you merely look at me.
NIV.21:
You turn on me ruthlessly;
with the might of your hand you attack me.
NIV.22:
You snatch me up and drive me before the wind;
you toss me about in the storm.
NIV.23:
I know you will bring me down to death,
to the place appointed for all the living.
NIV.24:
“Surely no one lays a hand on a broken man
when he cries for help in his distress.
NIV.25:
Have I not wept for those in trouble?
Has not my soul grieved for the poor?
NIV.26:
Yet when I hoped for good, evil came;
when I looked for light, then came darkness.
NIV.27:
The churning inside me never stops;
days of suffering confront me.
NIV.28:
I go about blackened, but not by the sun;
I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
NIV.29:
I have become a brother of jackals,
a companion of owls.
NIV.30:
My skin grows black and peels;
my body burns with fever.
NIV.31:
My harp is tuned to mourning,
and my flute to the sound of wailing.

MSG.1:
"But no longer. Now I'm the butt of their jokes—
Young ruffians! whippersnappers!
MSG.2:
Why, I considered their fathers
mere inexperienced pups.
But they are worse than dogs—good for nothing,
stray, mangy animals,
MSG.3:
Half-starved, scavenging the back alleys,
howling at the moon;
MSG.4:
Homeless guttersnipes
chewing on old bones and licking old tin cans;
MSG.5:
Outcasts from the community,
cursed as dangerous delinquents.
MSG.6:
Nobody would put up with them;
they were driven from the neighborhood.
MSG.7:
You could hear them out there at the edge of town,
yelping and barking, huddled in junkyards,
MSG.8:
A gang of beggars and no-names,
thrown out on their ears.
MSG.9:
"But now I'm the one they're after,
mistreating me, taunting and mocking.
MSG.10:
They abhor me, they abuse me.
How dare those scoundrels—they spit in my face!
MSG.11:
Now that God has undone me and left me in a heap,
they hold nothing back. Anything goes.
MSG.12:
They come at me from my blind side,
trip me up, then jump on me while I'm down.
MSG.13:
They throw every kind of obstacle in my path,
determined to ruin me—
and no one lifts a finger to help me!
MSG.14:
They violate my broken body,
trample through the rubble of my ruined life.
MSG.15:
Terrors assault me—
my dignity in shreds,
salvation up in smoke.
MSG.16:
"And now my life drains out,
as suffering seizes and grips me hard.
MSG.17:
Night gnaws at my bones;
the pain never lets up.
MSG.18:
I am tied hand and foot, my neck in a noose.
I twist and turn.
MSG.19:
Thrown facedown in the muck,
I'm a muddy mess, inside and out.
MSG.20:
"I shout for help, God, and get nothing, no answer!
I stand to face you in protest, and you give me a blank stare!
MSG.21:
You've turned into my tormenter—
you slap me around, knock me about.
MSG.22:
You raised me up so I was riding high
and then dropped me, and I crashed.
MSG.23:
I know you're determined to kill me,
to put me six feet under.
MSG.24:
"What did I do to deserve this?
Did I ever hit anyone who was calling for help?
MSG.25:
Haven't I wept for those who live a hard life,
been heartsick over the lot of the poor?
MSG.26:
But where did it get me?
I expected good but evil showed up.
I looked for light but darkness fell.
MSG.27:
My stomach's in a constant churning, never settles down.
Each day confronts me with more suffering.
MSG.28:
I walk under a black cloud. The sun is gone.
I stand in the congregation and protest.
MSG.29:
I howl with the jackals,
I hoot with the owls.
MSG.30:
I'm black and blue all over,
burning up with fever.
MSG.31:
My fiddle plays nothing but the blues;
my mouth harp wails laments.

NRSVCE.1:
“But now they make sport of me,
those who are younger than I,
whose fathers I would have disdained
to set with the dogs of my flock.
NRSVCE.2:
What could I gain from the strength of their hands?
All their vigor is gone.
NRSVCE.3:
Through want and hard hunger
they gnaw the dry and desolate ground,
NRSVCE.4:
they pick mallow and the leaves of bushes,
and to warm themselves the roots of broom.
NRSVCE.5:
They are driven out from society;
people shout after them as after a thief.
NRSVCE.6:
In the gullies of wadis they must live,
in holes in the ground, and in the rocks.
NRSVCE.7:
Among the bushes they bray;
under the nettles they huddle together.
NRSVCE.8:
A senseless, disreputable brood,
they have been whipped out of the land.
NRSVCE.9:
“And now they mock me in song;
I am a byword to them.
NRSVCE.10:
They abhor me, they keep aloof from me;
they do not hesitate to spit at the sight of me.
NRSVCE.11:
Because God has loosed my bowstring and humbled me,
they have cast off restraint in my presence.
NRSVCE.12:
On my right hand the rabble rise up;
they send me sprawling,
and build roads for my ruin.
NRSVCE.13:
They break up my path,
they promote my calamity;
no one restrains them.
NRSVCE.14:
As through a wide breach they come;
amid the crash they roll on.
NRSVCE.15:
Terrors are turned upon me;
my honor is pursued as by the wind,
and my prosperity has passed away like a cloud.
NRSVCE.16:
“And now my soul is poured out within me;
days of affliction have taken hold of me.
NRSVCE.17:
The night racks my bones,
and the pain that gnaws me takes no rest.
NRSVCE.18:
With violence he seizes my garment;
he grasps me by the collar of my tunic.
NRSVCE.19:
He has cast me into the mire,
and I have become like dust and ashes.
NRSVCE.20:
I cry to you and you do not answer me;
I stand, and you merely look at me.
NRSVCE.21:
You have turned cruel to me;
with the might of your hand you persecute me.
NRSVCE.22:
You lift me up on the wind, you make me ride on it,
and you toss me about in the roar of the storm.
NRSVCE.23:
I know that you will bring me to death,
and to the house appointed for all living.
NRSVCE.24:
“Surely one does not turn against the needy,
when in disaster they cry for help.
NRSVCE.25:
Did I not weep for those whose day was hard?
Was not my soul grieved for the poor?
NRSVCE.26:
But when I looked for good, evil came;
and when I waited for light, darkness came.
NRSVCE.27:
My inward parts are in turmoil, and are never still;
days of affliction come to meet me.
NRSVCE.28:
I go about in sunless gloom;
I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
NRSVCE.29:
I am a brother of jackals,
and a companion of ostriches.
NRSVCE.30:
My skin turns black and falls from me,
and my bones burn with heat.
NRSVCE.31:
My lyre is turned to mourning,
and my pipe to the voice of those who weep.
